title: defect-claim/v2
description: nodes/<id>/defects/<timestamp>-<contributor>.yaml, or targets/<id>/defs/defects/<timestamp>-<contributor>.yaml (D-16; F08-R7; F12-R4, Q7): a statement-defect claim, free and shaped. v2 (2026-09-12) adds one class value, `screen-finding`: the QA screen's own claim (F12-R3, R4), which carries a kernel-checked exhibit and names both readings — misformalization (D-8) or refutation (D-12) — without asserting either; a curator routes it by appending a claim whose `routes` names this file, with the D-16 class they chose or the `refutation` reading. `screen-finding` is a routing state, not a class: it enters no per-class measurement (D-11). A screen-finding claim names the exhibit file it rests on in `qa_exhibit` (F12-R15: trusted by content). Everything else is v1's: pre-triage in the service and the gate (D-35), the exhibit elaborating in the sandbox (C9), adjudication D-17's. v1 stays live and unedited (D-34); the service files classed claims at v1, only the screen files v2.

stmt_ref.description: the node id whose Statement.lean is claimed defective, or defs/<file>.lean under the target

qa_exhibit.description: For a screen-finding claim: the path, relative to the graph root, of the exhibit file under targets/<id>/qa/exhibits/ that the QA record cites (F12-R15). Null on any other claim.

readings.description: For a screen-finding claim: the two things a derived falsehood can mean, named so nobody has to remember; the claim asserts neither (F12-R4, D-9 v3.12).

routes.description: A curator's routing of an earlier screen-finding claim in the same directory: which file, and which reading. With `misformalization` this claim's own class is the D-16 class the curator chose and a D-8 revision follows; with `refutation` the finding is a D-12 counterexample in waiting and this claim's class is whatever best describes the exhibit.

note.description: Free text; capped and served as untrusted data (F12 §7).
